summary: This article explains why sharks are fish to respect rather than monsters to fear: their many kinds, teeth, senses, rare bites, and important role in a healthy ocean.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Sharks: Misunderstood Hunters” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: a strong but bendy material in the body that is softer than bone
tiny plants and animals that float and drift in water

challengeTerms.def: at the very top; an apex predator has no natural hunters
small, quick movements back and forth that can travel through water, air, or ground
what most people believe or say about someone or something

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that sharks are more dangerous to people than people are to sharks? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how sharks help keep the ocean in balance.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review species, cartilage, and plankton, and let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses apex, vibrations, and reputation to explain one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
